title: Renal Clinical Evidence Blueprint v1
description: Extension-only manifest. Does NOT create a new disease, variant, or PPS/KPS definition -- 'Acute Renal Failure' and 'Chronic Renal Failure' (both under the Renal System body system, PR #40, merged) already exist as two DISTINCT (non-mirrored) disease identities with different existing concept sets. Chronic Renal Failure already contains Uremia, Oliguria, Intractable Hyperkalemia (as 'Intractable Hyperkalemia Greater Than 7.0' / 'Intractable Hyperkalemia Not Responsive To Treatment'), Uremic Pericarditis, and Hepatorenal Syndrome; Acute Renal Failure does not. Both diseases already contain 'Not Seeking Dialysis' and 'Discontinuing Dialysis' treatment-state variants (clinically equivalent to 'Dialysis Refused' / 'Dialysis Discontinued'). This manifest therefore extends BOTH diseases WITHOUT forcing symmetry -- it adds only what is genuinely missing per disease: (1) 5 atomic FINDING concepts (Uremia, Oliguria, Intractable Hyperkalemia, Uremic Pericarditis, Hepatorenal Syndrome) added ONLY to Acute Renal Failure, which lacks them; (2) 1 new HOSPICE_ELIGIBILITY_SUPPORT concept (Not Candidate For Dialysis) added to BOTH diseases, since neither has a concept for a treating clinician's determination that the patient is not a dialysis candidate (distinct from the patient's own refusal, already covered by 'Not Seeking Dialysis'); (3) cross-disease OntologyRelationship edges linking each disease's existing PPS Less Than 70 Percent / KPS Less Than 70 Percent concepts to the Functional Assessment Framework v1 (PR #49, merged) scale-definition concepts, without duplicating the scale content; (4) a recertification evidence trend model (9 PROGNOSTIC_INDICATOR concepts covering GFR/Creatinine/Potassium/PPS/KPS/Weight/Hospitalization/Symptom/Narrative trend) applied identically to both diseases; (5) a documentation-only AI capability boundary (ai_may / ai_may_not), mirroring the pattern already established in the Functional Assessment Framework v1, CHF, Dementia, and Pulmonary Clinical Evidence Blueprint manifests. No schema, migration, or API changes. No existing PR #40 or PR #49 row is ever modified, renamed, or duplicated.

already_present_verified.note: Uremia, Oliguria, Intractable Hyperkalemia, Uremic Pericarditis, Hepatorenal Syndrome, 'Not Seeking Dialysis', and 'Discontinuing Dialysis' were verified already present in PR #40's Chronic Renal Failure disease (and the dialysis-related two in Acute Renal Failure as well) under an identical or clinically-equivalent name. No duplicate concept was created for any of these.

mapping.existing_concept: Intractable Hyperkalemia Greater Than 7.0 / Intractable Hyperkalemia Not Responsive To Treatment (Chronic Renal Failure only)

mapping.requested: GFR Trend / Creatinine Trend / Potassium Trend
mapping.existing_concept: GFR Less Than 15 mL/min / Serum Creatinine Greater Than 8.0 mg/dL / Serum Potassium Greater Than 7.0 (static thresholds only, not trend concepts -- these remain distinct and are not duplicated by the new trend indicators below)

new_concepts.name: Uremia
new_concepts.description: Clinical syndrome of toxin accumulation due to severe loss of renal function, producing symptoms such as nausea, confusion, and pruritus -- present in PR #40's Chronic Renal Failure disease but genuinely absent from Acute Renal Failure.

new_concepts.name: Oliguria
new_concepts.description: Urine output below the threshold expected for adequate renal clearance, a hallmark finding of severe/advancing renal failure -- present in PR #40's Chronic Renal Failure disease but genuinely absent from Acute Renal Failure.

new_concepts.name: Intractable Hyperkalemia
new_concepts.description: Elevated serum potassium that persists despite treatment, a life-threatening complication of severe renal failure -- present in PR #40's Chronic Renal Failure disease (as 'Intractable Hyperkalemia Greater Than 7.0' / 'Intractable Hyperkalemia Not Responsive To Treatment') but genuinely absent from Acute Renal Failure.

new_concepts.name: Uremic Pericarditis
new_concepts.description: Pericardial inflammation caused by uremic toxin accumulation, a serious complication of advanced renal failure -- present in PR #40's Chronic Renal Failure disease but genuinely absent from Acute Renal Failure.

new_concepts.name: Hepatorenal Syndrome
new_concepts.description: Progressive renal failure occurring in the context of severe liver disease, reflecting profound circulatory dysfunction -- present in PR #40's Chronic Renal Failure disease but genuinely absent from Acute Renal Failure.

new_concepts.name: Not Candidate For Dialysis
new_concepts.description: A treating clinician's determination that the patient is not medically appropriate for dialysis, distinct from the patient's own informed refusal (already captured by the existing 'Not Seeking Dialysis' concept/variant) -- genuinely absent from both diseases.

functional_assessment_linkage.description: Links each Renal disease's existing PPS Less Than 70 Percent hospice-eligibility-support concept to the Functional Assessment Framework's PPS scale definition for full nurse-facing score interpretation, without duplicating the scale's level content.

Links each Renal disease's existing KPS Less Than 70 Percent hospice-eligibility-support concept to the Functional Assessment Framework's KPS scale definition for full nurse-facing score interpretation, without duplicating the scale's level content.

trend_indicators.name: GFR Trend
trend_indicators.description: Comparison of the patient's glomerular filtration rate between the previous and current certification periods, documenting progressive renal decline.

trend_indicators.name: Creatinine Trend
trend_indicators.description: Comparison of the patient's serum creatinine between the previous and current certification periods, documenting progressive renal decline.

trend_indicators.name: Potassium Trend
trend_indicators.description: Comparison of the patient's serum potassium between the previous and current certification periods, documenting worsening or refractory hyperkalemia.

trend_indicators.name: PPS Trend
trend_indicators.description: Comparison of the patient's previous PPS score to the current PPS score at recertification; a decreasing score supports continued functional-decline documentation.

trend_indicators.name: KPS Trend
trend_indicators.description: Comparison of the patient's previous KPS score to the current KPS score at recertification; a decreasing score supports continued functional-decline documentation.

trend_indicators.name: Weight Trend
trend_indicators.description: Comparison of the patient's weight between the previous and current certification periods, documenting unintentional weight loss or fluid-related weight change.

trend_indicators.name: Hospitalization Trend
trend_indicators.description: Comparison of the frequency of renal-related hospitalizations between the previous and current certification periods, documenting recurrent hospitalization.

trend_indicators.name: Symptom Trend
trend_indicators.description: Comparison of overall renal-failure symptom burden (uremia, pruritus, fluid overload, fatigue) between the previous and current certification periods.

trend_indicators.name: Narrative Trend
trend_indicators.description: A structured narrative summary comparing the patient's overall clinical course between the previous and current certification periods, supporting the physician's recertification determination.

differentiation_guards: This manifest never creates a new OntologyDisease, OntologyDiseaseFamily, or OntologyBodySystem row -- it resolves the existing Acute Renal Failure, Chronic Renal Failure, and Functional Assessment Framework diseases by exact name and aborts if any is missing.
This manifest never creates a new OntologyDiseaseVariant row.
This manifest never creates a duplicate PPS/KPS definition -- it links to PR #40's and PR #49's existing rows via OntologyRelationship only.

This manifest does NOT force symmetry between Acute Renal Failure and Chronic Renal Failure -- each disease receives only the new_concepts entries whose 'diseases' list names it, reflecting that PR #40 built them as genuinely distinct (non-mirrored) disease identities.

Renal clinical evidence and functional assessments support functional status documentation, clinical decline documentation, recertification review, and clinical picture development; they do not independently establish diagnosis, prognosis, hospice eligibility, or terminal status.
